Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We're ready to lock down the network details for the Redwood Private deployment in our staging VPC so your team can start the tenant attachment work next week. High-level ask below — please confirm whether any of these are blockers on your side: 

- Control-plane allowlist: we can allocate a /29 (two usable IPs + NAT) for Redwood control-plane endpoints. Can you confirm the exact IPs to expect or whether you'll use dynamic egress from multiple AZs?
- Data-plane peering: prefer static routes for now; we can open BGP later. Any preference from Redwood?
- MTLS & port list: we'll need the port/protocols that must be allowed through our perimeter (we have a tight firewall ruleset).
- Audit evidence: we will need a short reference diagram and a checklist to hand to our security team for the onboarding ticket (JIRA RDW-4521).

Attached: acme-tenant-onboarding-v1.pdf (pdf) — contains tenant details and contact points, onboarding_network_map.png (image).

Can you loop in your network lead so we can get a recommended CIDR and port list? We'd like to target the peering cutover on Thursday (2026-09-16) if that works.

Best,

Subject: RE: SEGOPS: Tenant peering & attachment details for Redwood Private

Sabrina / Marissa — technical details below, written to be actionable for Acme's networking team. I've attached a lightweight reference diagram and the segops runbook snippet.

Summary (recommendations):
- Control-plane egress: allocate a /29 public block. We will use two public IPs for control-plane endpoints (one active, one standby) and NAT for additional outbound if needed.
- Ports/protocols:
  - TCP 443: HTTPS (control-plane REST & cert exchange)
  - TCP 7443: mTLS control RPCs (Redwood internal; client-auth mandatory)
  - TCP 10250: optional metrics/agent (only if you enable host-level telemetry)
- Peering: start with static routes on your side (advertise the tenant range to Redwood’s NAT IP). For production we can flip to BGP (we support eBGP peering with MD5 on request).
- TLS & certs: Redwood will present mTLS client certs; you must allow SNI for hostnames redwood-control-*.redwood.local (we'll provide full CN/SANs).

Acceptance checklist for cutover (short):
1) Acme opens ports above to the two control-plane IPs (we will provide them in a follow-up email once allocated).
2) Test control-plane handshake: successful mTLS client auth from Redwood to the provided endpoints.
3) Data-plane verification: simple curl of data-plane ingress and verification of token exchange — Marcus will supply the token test command.

Attachments included: redwood-private-peering-ref.svg (diagram), segops-runbook-v0.3.md (runbook snippet). Link to internal ref: https://redwood.app/drive/teams/netops/private-peering-ref/RED-PEER-ACME
